Subject: Hyperscaler delta & Opsuite qualification — post-demo follow-up

Thanks again for the time today, Samir — great conversation and appreciates the level of detail from your ops team. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can scope a side-by-side evaluation vs the hyperscaler endpoints you mentioned.

Key takeaway (short): Redwood's opsuite + runtime tends to lower effective per-1M-token spend by combining:
- automatic KV/prefix caching (transparent, no code changes)
- workload-aware batching with configurable p99 latency targets
- quantized model variants for steady-state unit-costs

Initial illustrative economics (assumptions below):
- Hyperscaler managed endpoints (baseline): ~$21–25 per 1M tokens (no caching assumptions).
- Redwood Hosted (no caching, default batching): ~$14 per 1M tokens.
- Redwood Hosted (with caching at ~60% hit + batching): effective ~$8.5–10 per 1M tokens.
- Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity, quantized): ~$5.5–7 per 1M tokens (higher upfront commit).

Assumptions: medium sequence length ~350 tokens, model = M-size LLM you demoed, 60% prefix reuse for typical flows you described. These are ballpark numbers to guide tests — we'll validate with your sample prompts.

Proposed test matrix (please confirm):
1) Prompt set run: you provide ~10k representative prompts (anonymized) — we run 1M token equivalent and report token distribution, average seq len, and cacheability.
2) Cache hit sensitivity: simulate runs at 0/30/60/85% cache hit and show effective per-1M token costs and latency p50/p95/p99 at batch sizes 1/8/32.
3) Hyperscaler parity run: we (or you) run the same dataset against the hyperscaler endpoint you nominate (we can also run if you provide a short-lived test account) to capture latency and cost per-1M tokens.
4) Ops and SLOs: measure p99 latency under a 100 RPS sustained window + 300 RPS burst to validate autoscale behavior.

Attachments: acme-eval-promptset.csv (template), redwood-cost-model-v1.xlsx (cost assumptions), bench-runbook.md (bench steps).

Next actions / owners: 
- Samir: confirm prompt set and whether Acme will run competitor side or provide test account (due Fri 9/24).
- Ben: lead bench runs once sample is in (internal owner).
- Laura: prepare SOC2 / security note for procurement thread.

Happy to jump on a 30-min ops call with your infra folks next week to walk the bench plan.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Samir — good questions. Short answers and clarifications below, plus we mapped out the specific artifacts your team requested.

1) Measurement methodology
- Per-1M-token numbers: base compute + gpu amortization + software infra (autoscaler, orchestration) + service margin. For Hosted numbers we include multi-tenant infra cost; for Dedicated we model reserved GPU amortization across committed capacity. We flag assumptions in the attached redwood-cost-model-v1.xlsx so you can tweak commit size and seq-length.

2) Who runs the hyperscaler parity run
- Preferred: Acme runs hyperscaler endpoint (ops sets creds) and shares run outputs (latency logs + cost numbers). Reason: avoids cross-account billing and gives us raw hyperscaler logs for parity comparison. If you prefer, we can run both sides if you provide a short-lived role. Happy either way — note the bench-runbook.md includes both options.

3) Compliance checklist (quick)
- SOC2 Type II: yes (audit report available on request)
- Data residency & KMS: supported for Dedicated + Private deployments (we'll provide integrations doc).
Laura, can you attach a one-pager SOC2 summary for procurement?

Bench details (Ben will lead):
- Runs to execute: 2x 1M-token passes (no-cache), 3x cache-sensitivity runs (0/50/80%), batch sizes 1/8/32. Capture tokenized distribution, p50/p95/p99 latency, and effective cost per 1M tokens (raw and with cache).
- Measurement notes: we instrument both token-level time and request-level latencies; compute effective cost with your real token mix.
- Timeline: bench kickoff once we have prompts — target readout Wed 9/30 (internal) and preliminary parity summary by Fri 10/2.

Action items (updated):
- Samir: deliver anonymized prompt set + confirm who runs hyperscaler side (due Thu 9/24)
- Ben: prepare bench infra and instrumentation (internal, in-flight)
- Laura: SOC2 one-pager + security contact (internal)

I'll block a 30-min sync for Wed 9/30 10:00 PT unless you prefer a different slot.

Thanks,
Marissa
